replies.author: @tonychen76
replies.text: @randomtravels2024 Hi, I'm Indonesian. The following can be hard for non-Indonesians to understand. The argument that the Papuans have no connection to the rest of Indonesia is false and irrelevant. It's false because Indonesia isn't just Java. Rather it's a huge conglomeration of many ethnicities and it's more like a gradual change rather than a sharp boundary. The West Papuans did not have direct connection to, say, the Acehnese, but Moluccans traded with coastal Papuans since forever and coastal Papuans traded with mountain Papuans while Moluccans traded with the Bugis and the Bugis traded with the Javanese and Malays. So yes, if you take a native Javanese with a native Papuan and put them side by side they're pretty different, but take all the ethnicities living in western, central, and eastern Indonesia and put everyone together and we start to see how they relate to each other. It's also irrelevant because we don't use race, culture, religion, nor heritage as the basis in determining what is Indonesia or who is Indonesian. We don't define Indonesian as Javanese or Malays or Ambonese or Papuans. We don't define it as Muslims or Hindu or Christians or Traditional Belief or whatever.  One is Indonesian first and race, heritage, religion, culture are all secondary. Our founding fathers explicitly said all Indonesians are one. Now, that doesn't mean that we don't have problems with racism. Trust me, I've been on the receiving end of it myself. But we are not supposed to be racist, and that's why to us, the idea that Papuans are not supposed to be Indonesians because they're different is nonsensical.
